title: Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh Win India's First-Ever Judo Gold Medals at Commonwealth Games
excerpt: India made judo history at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games as Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh claimed gold in the 48 kg and 60 kg categories on the same day.
body:
• Asmita Dey won the women's 48 kg judo gold, becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.
  • Harsh Singh dominated the men's 60 kg category, winning all four bouts to claim gold.
  • Yamini Mourya added a silver in the women's 57 kg, giving India three medals on the opening day of judo at Glasgow 2026.
  • India finished tied with Canada at the top of the judo medal table with two golds and one silver.

India rewrote its judo history at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Thursday, with Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh both winning gold medals — the country's first ever in the sport at the Games.

A Historic Double on Day One

Dey, a 23-year-old from Tripura competing in the women's 48 kg category, powered through three opponents at the SEC Centre to reach the final against Canada's Heidi Quach. In a tense gold medal bout, Dey prevailed 2s1–1 to etch her name in Indian sporting history.

"I was sure I would win. I came here with that belief."

— Asmita Dey, India's first judo gold medallist at the Commonwealth Games

The victory carried deep personal significance. Dey's father, who repaired bicycles for a living earning around Rs 300 per day, passed away from a stroke just seven months before the Games. She dedicated the medal to his memory and to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, according to Zee News.

Harsh Singh's Dominant Run

Hours earlier, Harsh Singh had already given India its first taste of judo gold. The 60 kg judoka, seeded fourth, dominated every round. He opened with a commanding ippon victory over Malawi's Chikondi Kathewera, then dispatched Vanuatu's Alan Monthouel before beating Australia's top-seeded Pedro Neto in the semifinal.

In the final against Australia's Joshua Katz, Singh was clinical, winning 10–0 to secure the gold. His path through the draw was marked by aggressive, attacking judo that left opponents with little room to counter.

Yamini Mourya's Silver Caps a Landmark Day

The medals kept coming for India as Yamini Mourya reached the 57 kg final with dominant wins over Ghana's Agyei and South Africa's Breytenbach, both by ippon. She fell to England's Acelya Toprak in the gold medal bout but took home silver — adding to what was already India's best-ever day in Commonwealth Games judo.

By the close of Day 1, India sat tied with Canada atop the judo medal table with two golds and one silver from three medals overall.

India's Rising Judo Program

The breakthrough results reflect a concerted effort by the Sports Authority of India (SAI), which had trained four of India's Glasgow judokas at its Centre of Excellence in Bhopal. Dey, a product of the Khelo India University Games system, had previously won gold at the 2025 Casablanca African Open and a silver at the 2023 Asian Open in Kuwait.

For the Indian diaspora watching worldwide, the double gold marks a milestone in a sport where India has historically struggled against established powers like Japan, France, and South Korea. The CWG provided a platform where India's emerging talent could compete and win — and they seized it.

What's Next

Judo competition continues through August 2 in Glasgow, with India fielding athletes in five more weight categories across men's and women's events. If the opening day is any indication, more medals could follow as India's judo program continues its rapid ascent.
